entry = await rlm.harness.create_memory(title='ARC: Orient embedded pattern by external color markers', path='arc/tasks', global_=True, content='For ARC tasks with a solid 1 rectangle containing an internal pattern plus three unique colored marker cells (e.g. 2/3/4) and matching singletons outside, the external marker arrangement indicates the target arrangement of those marker colors in the output. Transform the full rectangle (including pattern/background) by the corresponding reflection/transpose so the internal markers align spatially with the external arrangement; output is the transformed rectangle, with exterior pixels omitted. Determine orientation from marker layout, not color identity alone. Examples: if internal marker colors occupy TL,TR,BR but external target swaps TL and BR while TR stays, use anti-diagonal reflection (for source h×w, (r,c)->(w-1-c,h-1-r), giving w×h output); if target arrangement is main-diagonal transpose, use (r,c)->(c,r). Carefully transcribe all pattern cells—one omitted cell caused the first incorrect submission in this instance. In solved test, 13×10 inner rectangle transformed by anti-diagonal reflection to 10×13; external colors 8 TL,2 TR,4 BR set orientation, matching transformed inner markers. Output grid preserved the 1 background and all embedded colors. Demo caveat: output marker positions sometimes appeared offset by one from naive boundary expectations, so prioritize matching the transform of the embedded pattern and verify boundary coordinates against given demonstrations.' )
print(entry)
